reason: The cited evidence confirms that Al2O3 and SiO2 are protective due to low diffusivities (E2) and that scale cracking/spallation can occur from thermal expansion mismatch (E3), but it does not provide specific data on diffusion rates, oxygen permeability, or oxide characteristics for Mn, Al, or Si in CrFeCoNiX alloys, nor does it directly compare these elements under the proposed conditions.
premises: Al or Si form thin, coherent, protective Al2O3 or SiO2 scales due to lower oxygen permeability and slower outward diffusion
Mn forms thick, mixed Mn-rich oxides and spinels prone to cracking and spallation due to faster diffusion and higher reactivity
Al2O3 and SiO2 scales are protective at high temperatures (>900 °C) because of low diffusivities and high stability
Oxide scale cracking and spallation arise from internal stresses due to volumetric mismatch and thermal expansion differences
The element X (Al, Si, Mn) in CrFeCoNiX controls the nature and stability of the oxide scale
